# Model loading and comparison

```{r}
# Load the models dynamically based on available RDS files
fit_base   <- if (file.exists("../fits/base_fit_marking_type.rds")) readRDS("../fits/base_fit_marking_type.rds") else NULL
fit_k10    <- if (file.exists("../fits/base_fit_marking_type_k10.rds")) readRDS("../fits/base_fit_marking_type_k10.rds") else NULL
fit_tensor <- if (file.exists("../fits/tensor_fit_marking_type_k10.rds")) readRDS("../fits/tensor_fit_marking_type_k10.rds") else NULL
fit_tensor_k4 <- if (file.exists("../fits/tensor_fit_marking_type_k4.rds")) readRDS("../fits/tensor_fit_marking_type_k4.rds") else NULL
fit_tensor_k10_token <- if (file.exists("../fits/tensor_fit_marking_type_k10_token.rds")) readRDS("../fits/tensor_fit_marking_type_k10_token.rds") else NULL
fit_tensor_k4_token <- if (file.exists("../fits/tensor_fit_marking_type_k4_token.rds")) readRDS("../fits/tensor_fit_marking_type_k4_token.rds") else NULL

# Put them in a named list for easier iteration
models <- purrr::compact(list(
  "Base (k=4)" = fit_base,
  "Base (k=10)" = fit_k10,
  "Tensor (k=10)" = fit_tensor,
  "Tensor (k=4)" = fit_tensor_k4,
  "Tensor (k=10) Token" = fit_tensor_k10_token,
  "Tensor (k=4) Token" = fit_tensor_k4_token
))

# Identify best-performing primary model (Model 5: Tensor Token k=10)
fit_primary <- if (!is.null(fit_tensor_k10_token)) fit_tensor_k10_token else fit_tensor
```

```{r}
# Compute LOO for each model and compare
# Warning: This step might take a few moments depending on model size.
loo_list <- map(models, loo)

# loo_compare() keeps the names when it is handed the *list*. The earlier
# do.call(..., unname(loo_list)) form dropped them, so every row of the
# comparison printed as `.x[[i]]` and the ranking could not be read off it.
comparison <- loo_compare(loo_list)

```

```{r}
print(comparison, simplify = FALSE)
```

# MCMC Convergence Diagnostics

```{r mcmc-diagnostics}
if (file.exists("../analysis/reports/mcmc_convergence.csv")) {
  mcmc_diag_list <- read.csv("../analysis/reports/mcmc_convergence.csv")
} else {
  mcmc_diag_list <- map2_dfr(models, names(models), function(fit, m_name) {
    stan_fit <- fit$fit
    divs <- rstan::get_num_divergent(stan_fit)
    max_td <- rstan::get_num_max_treedepth(stan_fit)
    
    rhats <- brms::rhat(fit)
    max_rhat <- max(rhats, na.rm = TRUE)
    pct_rhat_ok <- mean(rhats <= 1.01, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
    
    draws <- posterior::as_draws(fit)
    d_sum <- posterior::summarise_draws(draws)
    min_bulk <- min(d_sum$ess_bulk, na.rm = TRUE)
    min_tail <- min(d_sum$ess_tail, na.rm = TRUE)
    
    data.frame(
      Model = m_name,
      Max_Rhat = round(max_rhat, 4),
      Pct_Rhat_LE_1.01 = sprintf("%.1f%%", pct_rhat_ok),
      Min_Bulk_ESS = round(min_bulk, 0),
      Min_Tail_ESS = round(min_tail, 0),
      Divergences = divs,
      Max_Treedepth_Hits = max_td,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })
}

knitr::kable(
  mcmc_diag_list,
  col.names = c("Model", "Max R-hat", "R-hat <= 1.01 (%)", "Min Bulk-ESS", "Min Tail-ESS", "Divergences", "Max Treedepth Hits"),
  caption = "MCMC Convergence Diagnostics Summary"
)
```




# Fixed effects
```{r}
# Extract fixed effects draws for all models
extract_fixed_draws <- function(model, model_name) {
  model %>%
    gather_draws(`^b_[^s].*`, regex = TRUE) %>% # Exclude spline terms
    mutate(Model = model_name)
}

all_fixed_draws <- map2_dfr(models, names(models), extract_fixed_draws)

ggplot(all_fixed_draws, aes(x = .value, y = .variable, color = Model)) +
  stat_pointinterval(position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  labs(
    title = "Posterior Distributions of Fixed Effects Across Models",
    x = "Estimate (Log-Odds)",
    y = "Predictor"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
# Extract fixed effects draws for the primary best-performing model (Model 5)
tensor_fixed_draws <- fit_primary %>%
  gather_draws(`^b_.*`, regex = TRUE) %>%
  filter(!grepl("^b_(s|t2)date", .variable)) %>%
  mutate(
    # Rename variables to human-readable format
    .variable = case_when(
      .variable == "b_Intercept" ~ "Intercept (Unipartite Vowel Base)",
      .variable == "b_marking_typevowel_bipartite" ~ "Marking: Bipartite Vowel",
      .variable == "b_log_token_freq" ~ "Token Frequency (Log)",
      .variable == "b_log_freq" ~ "Lemma Frequency (Log)",
      .variable == "b_has_alt_presno" ~ "Alt. Absence: Present/Past Sg",
      .variable == "b_has_alt_presyes" ~ "Alt. Presence: Present/Past Sg",
      .variable == "b_has_alt_pastno" ~ "Alt. Absence: Past Sg/Past Pl",
      .variable == "b_has_alt_pastyes" ~ "Alt. Presence: Past Sg/Past Pl",
      .variable == "b_log_alt_pres_freq" ~ "Alt. Type Frequency: Present (Log)",
      .variable == "b_log_alt_past_freq" ~ "Alt. Type Frequency: Past (Log)",
      .variable == "b_std_inflPastSg" ~ "Past Singular Context",
      .variable == "b_marking_typevowel_bipartite:std_inflPastSg" ~ "Bipartite Vowel × Past Singular Context",
      TRUE ~ .variable # Fallback for any unmapped variables
    )
  )

# Define the desired order of variables for the y-axis (top to bottom)
var_order <- c(
  "Bipartite Vowel × Past Singular Context",
  "Past Singular Context",
  "Marking: Bipartite Vowel",
  "Alt. Type Frequency: Past (Log)",
  "Alt. Type Frequency: Present (Log)",
  "Alt. Absence: Past Sg/Past Pl",
  "Alt. Presence: Past Sg/Past Pl",
  "Alt. Absence: Present/Past Sg",
  "Alt. Presence: Present/Past Sg",
  "Token Frequency (Log)",
  "Lemma Frequency (Log)",
  "Intercept (Unipartite Vowel Base)"
)

# Apply factor levels to control plotting order
tensor_fixed_draws <- tensor_fixed_draws %>%
  filter(!is.na(.variable)) %>%
  mutate(.variable = factor(.variable, levels = intersect(var_order, unique(.variable))))

# Generate the plot
ggplot(tensor_fixed_draws, aes(x = .value, y = .variable)) +
  stat_pointinterval(color = "blue", .width = c(0.66, 0.95)) + # Use a distinct single color; adjust .width as needed
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  labs(
    title = "",
    x = "Log-Odds",
    y = ""
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 15)),
    axis.text.y = element_text(color = "black"),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank()
  )

ggsave(
  filename = "../figures/fixed_effects.pdf", 
  plot = last_plot(),
  width = 10,       # Width in inches
  height = 7,      # Height in inches
  units = "in",
  device = cairo_pdf # Use cairo for better font embedding
)
```

```{r}
# Test Paul's Principle: bipartite vowel marking has lower log-odds of leveling relative to unipartite control baseline
hyp_paul <- hypothesis(fit_primary, "marking_typevowel_bipartite < 0")
print(hyp_paul)
```

```{r plot-bipartite-contrast, fig.width=12, fig.height=8}
# Plot the dynamic difference (contrast) between Bipartite and Unipartite marking
p_diff <- plot_comparisons(
  fit_primary,
  variables = list(marking_type = c("vowel_unipartite", "vowel_bipartite")),
  condition = c("date", "variety"),
  re_formula = NULL 
) +
  facet_wrap(~ variety, ncol = 1) +
  # Force both the line color and the ribbon fill to be blue
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Central German" = "blue", "Upper German" = "blue")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Central German" = "blue", "Upper German" = "blue")) +
  # Add a baseline of 0
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Bipartite - Unipartite Probability"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none", 
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.spacing = unit(1, "lines")
  )

# Save the plot
ggsave(
  filename = "../figures/bi-uni_diff.pdf", 
  plot = p_diff,
  width = 10,       
  height = 9,      
  units = "in",
  device = cairo_pdf 
)
```

```{r}
# Set meaningful baseline for alternation presence (both present and past alternations present)
alt_conditions <- data.frame(
  has_alt_pres = factor("yes", levels = c("no", "yes")),
  has_alt_past = factor("yes", levels = c("no", "yes"))
)

conditional_effects(fit_base, effects = "date", conditions = alt_conditions)
conditional_effects(fit_k10, effects = "date", conditions = alt_conditions)
conditional_effects(fit_tensor, effects = "date", conditions = alt_conditions)
if (!is.null(fit_tensor_k10_token)) {
  conditional_effects(fit_tensor_k10_token, effects = "date", conditions = alt_conditions)
}
```

```{r}
eff_marking <- conditional_effects(fit_primary, effects = "date:marking_type")

# 1. Extract the data directly for more control
plot_data <- as.data.frame(eff_marking[[1]])

# 2. Pre-process names for cleaner plotting
plot_data$marking_type <- factor(plot_data$marking_type, 
                                 levels = c("vowel_bipartite", "vowel_unipartite"),
                                 labels = c("Bipartite vowel", "Unipartite vowel"))

# 3. Create the "Small Multiples" plot
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = date, y = estimate__, color = marking_type, fill = marking_type)) +
  # Add ribbons with low alpha so they don't distract
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower__, ymax = upper__), alpha = 0.2, color = NA) +
  # Add a thick line for the main trajectory
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  # Facet by marking type to separate the overlaps
  facet_wrap(~marking_type) +
  # Use a colorblind-friendly scale
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "plasma", end = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "plasma", end = 0.8) +
  # Set the Y-axis to 0-1
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  labs(
    title = "",
    y = "Probability of Leveling",
    x = "Date",
    color = "Marking Type",
    fill = "Marking Type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none", # Hide legend since facets are labeled
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

ggsave(
  filename = "../figures/leveling_trajectories.pdf", 
  plot = last_plot(),
  width = 9,       # Width in inches
  height = 5,      # Height in inches
  units = "in",
  device = cairo_pdf # Use cairo for better font embedding
)
```

```{r}
if (!is.null(fit_tensor_k10_token)) {
  ce <- conditional_effects(
    fit_tensor_k10_token,

    surface = TRUE  # This generates a 2D heatmap/contour plot
  )
  plot(ce)
}
```

```{r}
# 1. Define a consistent temporal range starting from 1050
custom_date_range <- seq(1050, 1550, length.out = 100)

ce_base <- conditional_effects(
  fit_tensor,           
  effects = "date:log_freq",       
  surface = TRUE,
  int_conditions = list(date = custom_date_range)
)

df_base <- ce_base[["date:log_freq"]]       %>% 
  rename(log_frequency = log_freq)       %>% 
  mutate(model = "Log Lemma Frequency")

if (!is.null(fit_tensor_k10_token)) {
  # 2. Extract surface data, forcing predictions back to 1050 via int_conditions
  ce_k10  <- conditional_effects(
    fit_tensor_k10_token, 
    effects = "date:log_token_freq", 
    surface = TRUE,
    int_conditions = list(date = custom_date_range)
  )
  df_k10  <- ce_k10[["date:log_token_freq"]]  %>% 
    rename(log_frequency = log_token_freq) %>% 
    mutate(model = "Log Token Frequency")
  # 4. Combine the datasets to unify the grid space perfectly
  df_combined <- rbind(df_k10, df_base)
} else {
  df_combined <- df_base
}
```

```{r}
# 5. Generate the finalized plot with a filled surface
ggplot(df_combined, aes(x = date, y = log_frequency)) +
  # Use geom_tile instead of geom_raster to handle slightly uneven intervals natively
  geom_tile(aes(fill = estimate__)) + 
  
  # Overlay subtle contour lines
  geom_contour(aes(z = estimate__), color = "white", alpha = 0.4, linewidth = 0.8) +
  
  facet_wrap(~ model) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(1050, 1550, by = 100)
  ) +
  # Use coord_cartesian to set limits without throwing away edge data
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1050, 1550), expand = FALSE) + 
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = NULL, 
    fill = "Probability\nof levelling\n" 
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 1)) +  
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    # Increase the space between the two facets to prevent x-axis labels from overlapping
    panel.spacing = unit(1.5, "lines") 
  )


ggsave(
  filename = "../figures/freq_time.pdf", 
  plot = last_plot(),
  #device = "pdf",
  width = 14,       # Width in inches
  height = 8,      # Height in inches
  units = "in",
  device = cairo_pdf # Use cairo for better font embedding
)
```

```{r}
# Extract conditional effects for the continuous variables

  fit_primary, 
  effects = c(freq_var, "log_alt_pres_freq", "log_alt_past_freq")
)

# Customize the Frequency plot
p_freq <- plot(ce_freqs, plot = FALSE)[[freq_var]] +
  labs(
    title = if (freq_var == "log_token_freq") "Effect of Token Frequency" else "Effect of Lemma Frequency",
    x = if (freq_var == "log_token_freq") "Log Token Frequency" else "Log Frequency",
    y = "Probability of Leveling"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Customize the Present Alternation Frequency plot
p_alt_pres <- plot(ce_freqs, plot = FALSE)[["log_alt_pres_freq"]] +
  labs(
    title = "Alternation Freq (Present)",
    x = "Log Alt. Freq Pres. (Centered)",
    y = "Probability of Leveling"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Customize the Past Alternation Frequency plot
p_alt_past <- plot(ce_freqs, plot = FALSE)[["log_alt_past_freq"]] +
  labs(
    title = "Alternation Freq (Past)",
    x = "Log Alt. Freq Past (Centered)",
    y = "Probability of Leveling"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

p_freq
```

```{r}
# Calculate Average Marginal Effects for the categorical predictors
ame_cats <- avg_comparisons(
  fit_primary, 
  variables = c("marking_type", "std_infl", "has_alt_pres", "has_alt_past"),
  ndraws = 1000 # Increase to 4000 for final publication results
)

# Print a clean summary
print(ame_cats)

# Optional: Plot the marginal effects for marking_type specifically
plot_comparisons(
  fit_primary, 
  variables = "marking_type", 
  condition = "std_infl"
) +
  labs(
    title = "Contrasts of Marking Types",
    y = "Difference in Probability of Leveling",
    x = "Inflectional Slot"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
